messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High-rate NVRM/Xid errors detected on node gpu-17. Auto-paging oncall (level=prod, sev=2). Logs aggregated to /incidents/4512345678.

sara: seeing repeated Xid 13/31 and container restarts on gpu-17, started ~12:13UTC. Not sure if driver reset or hw ECC. Telemetry shows ECC correctable error spike.

ryan: looks like node is flapping - k8s reports repeated CrashLoopBackOff for inference pods pinned to GPU. Metrics: token latency spikes and 502s to frontend.

mike: I'll cordon and start evacuation for that node. tagging infra. Running:
```
kubectl cordon node/gpu-17
kubectl drain node/gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30 -n inference
```

janelle: customer-impact: CS reports 3 customers hitting timeouts around 12:15-12:18UTC. Most traffic routed to other region but a subset pinned to dedicated pool on gpu-17. Escalating to CS for customer bridge.

infra-bot: Node telemetry snapshot: gpu-17: ECC_CORRECTABLE=173, XID_ERRORS=42 in last 10m, nv-host-reset events=6. Kernel logs: see excerpt.
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (13, 0x00000001) submitted by pid=1842, pid_name=nvidia-persistenced
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679123] nvidia: ECE: uncorrectable ECC error at row 0x12 col 0x5
```

sara: those "fallen off the bus" messages are worrying. Might be intermittent PCIe link / riser or driver bug with this kernel combo. We should isolate node and avoid re-scheduling heavy long-running pods until root cause is known.

mike: drain completed for most pods but a couple of stateful sidecars refused termination due to local checkpoint files. Using --delete-local-data was needed. Post-drain, scheduler moved most traffic out.

oncall-sarah: taking handoff at 12:24UTC. @sara I'll lead triage with infra. @mike hold on a reboot until we collect nv-host and iostat. Noted. :eyes:

ryan: routing policy applied to avoid node-groups containing gpu-17; set routing override for 15m. Also flipped fallback routing to smaller quantized model for latency-sensitive tenants.
```
# temporary routing change
PATCH /routing/policies/serve-group-42
{ "prefer": ["model-small-v1","model-quant-q4_0"] }
```

janelle: customer-success: opening a bridge for the 3 affected customers, sending initial comms: "We're aware of elevated errors and have mitigations in place, will update in 30 mins." CS will provide list of request IDs for repro.

sara: collecting more logs. nv-host logs + dmesg + nvidia-smi diag. nvidia-smi shows GPU in Retried/Non-responsive state just before driver reset: 
```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ERRORS
GPU 0000:3b:00.0
  Xid Error Count                            : 42
  Retired Pages                             : 0
  Pending ECC Errors                        : multiple
```

infra-bot: quick health check (post-drain): cluster autoscaler did not kick; remaining capacity handled. No immediate OOM on other nodes but token latency elevated ~15%.

mike: executed soft driver restart sequence on node host (not full reboot):
```
sudo systemctl stop nvidia-persistenced
sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia
sudo modprobe nvidia nvidia_uvm
sudo systemctl start nvidia-persistenced
```
Observed one additional Xid during module rmmod then stable for ~90s but then Xid resumed.

sara: because it resumed, requesting full node reboot to clear possible hw state and PCI rescan. @infra-bot schedule reboot now if safe.

infra-bot: scheduled reboot for gpu-17 at 12:38UTC. Will cordon until reboot completes. Reboot reason: persistent Xid/ECC spike after soft-driver cycle.

oncall-sarah: logging customer impact summary into incident tracker: 3 customers, increased 5xx rate (peak +18%), ~120 failed requests, two long-running sessions dropped. Tagged P0 if customer bridge confirms revenue impact.

janelle: CS on bridge, customers are seeing intermittent failures but no data loss. They want ETA for full resolution and will request a postmortem.

ryan: putting a temporary circuit-breaker on heavy batch jobs to reduce GPU pressure cluster-wide. Also enabling more aggressive preemption for ephemeral pods so we don't refill the drained node immediately.

mike: reboot done at 12:47UTC. Node returned green but kernel logs still show some ECC corrected counts. Re-running stress tests for 10m to validate stability.

infra-bot: post-reboot telemetry: XID_ERRORS dropped to 0 for 7 minutes, ECC_CORRECTABLE decreased. Running health probe.

sara: running a controlled canary: allow small number of model-serving pods back onto gpu-17 (limit to 1 pod, low concurrency) and monitor for recurrence for 20m.

mike: canary scheduled, pods started. Monitoring telemetry and k8s events.

oncall-sarah: handoff notes for next shift: observed persistent Xid/ECC spike leading to driver resets and pod crashes. Actions taken: cordon & drain, soft-driver restart, full-node reboot, routing fallback, customer bridge opened, canary re-entry. Next steps: if Xid resurfaces -> escalate to hardware team for riser/PCIe inspection and decommission node if noisy; collect full nv-host dump + hw logs for vendor.

janelle: drafting customer update note and postmortem stub. Will include timelines and mitigations. CS will follow up with affected customers.

sara: adding remediation checklist to incident tracker: collect nv-host logs, iostat, pci-rescan trace, kernel dmesg, nvidia bugreport, and schedule hardware inspection if noise returns. Assigning to infra oncall: @ryan.

ryan: ack, will own follow-up. Will also add better autoscale cushion for dedicated pools to avoid single node hot-pinning in future.

customer-success: thanks, please also include request IDs we've provided so customers can correlate. We'll keep bridge open until you give all-clear. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated -> monitoring. Next update in 20m or on state change.
